title: The Choir of Caerlum
premise: Dominic Ravensworth, last apprentice of the Ravensworth smuggling guild, guides a desperate pilgrim through the Thornfell passes and discovers the old gods are answering prayers again — including the dragon-god Caerlum, whose dying flame the guild has secretly tended for generations. When Dominic learns her own bloodline is the key to either restoring or extinguishing that flame, she must choose between saving her found family of smugglers and honoring a covenant older than any kingdom. Hunted by an inquisitor who wants the gods dead for good, she carries the secret through war-torn valleys to the mountain's heart, where she reignites the fire at the cost of the guild's name and her own freedom. The book ends with the dragons waking, the guild dissolved but its people bound together as something new, and Dominic walking into exile as the first priestess the world has seen in three hundred years.
about_author: Odile Hartwell is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain communities before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who live in the gaps between laws, drawing on folklore collected during her travels.

chapters.title: Salt on the Pass
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She runs one final smuggling job through Thornfell before winter closes the passes, mourning the guild's decline after her mentor's death. A stranger named Ysolde begs passage, paying in old god-coins no mint has struck in centuries. Beat: weary competence shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Coin That Hums
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Examining the payment, Dominic finds the coins warm and faintly singing; her grandmother's journal hints the Ravensworths once served 'the Choir.' Ysolde reveals she seeks the dragon-fire shrine. Beat: unease curdling into forbidden curiosity.

chapters.title: What the Guild Kept
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. In the guildhall's cellar, Ysolde uncovers a sealed door only Ravensworth blood opens, revealing a sleeping hatchling-scale altar. Dominic realizes her family were not smugglers but keepers. Beat: betrayal of inherited lies.

chapters.title: Ashes Answer
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Praying half-mockingly at the altar, Dominic receives an answer — a voice like banked coals. The god Caerlum names her 'last chorister' and shows her a vision of the flame guttering. Beat: awe and terror entwined.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Road
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Serane Voss's POV. Voss arrives in the valley town hunting 'resurgent idolatry,' burning a shrine and interrogating locals. She learns a Ravensworth still lives. Beat: cold, methodical menace establishing the antagonist.

chapters.title: Found Kin
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic gathers the scattered guild remnants — hedge-witch Bramble, deaf tracker Osk, disgraced knight Pellam — warning them Voss is coming. They argue over fleeing versus fighting. Beat: fractious loyalty becoming family.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Dark
chapters.summary: Osk's POV. Osk leads them through a smuggler's tunnel while Voss's soldiers seal the passes above. He reflects on how the guild took him in when no one else would. Beat: quiet devotion amid danger.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Hollow Ford
chapters.summary: Pellam's POV. Cornered at a river crossing, Pellam trades information to Voss to save Bramble's life, then drowns his shame in confession to Dominic. Beat: guilt and the terrible arithmetic of survival.

chapters.title: Songs Older than Kingdoms
chapters.summary: Ysolde's POV. Ysolde reveals she is a remnant of the old priesthood, and the 'ancient war' was humans breaking their covenant with the dragons. She asks Dominic to carry the flame-secret south to the last roost. Beat: history reframed as wound.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Using Pellam's slip, Voss captures the guildhall and takes Bramble hostage, offering Dominic freedom in exchange for the altar's location. Beat: the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A prisoner swap goes wrong; Osk dies covering the escape, and Dominic burns the guildhall herself rather than let Voss desecrate it. Beat: rage, sacrifice, and the death of the old life.

chapters.title: Grief Is a Long Road
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The survivors trek south through thawing valleys; Bramble tends wounds and tempers Dominic's self-blame over Osk. Beat: mourning shared becomes love deepened.

chapters.title: The Roost of Embers
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. They reach the last roost: a canyon of petrified eggs and one ancient dragon, Vaelith, barely alive. Vaelith tests Dominic with the choir-song only a true keeper can hold. Beat: humility before vastness.

chapters.title: A Secret Too Heavy
chapters.summary: Pellam's POV. Pellam learns the flame can only be rekindled by a Ravensworth life freely given — and keeps it from Dominic, planning to offer himself instead. Beat: protective love shading into hubris.

chapters.title: Voss Ascendant
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Voss, reinforced and zealous, marches on the roost, believing destroying the last dragon will end plague and famine blamed on the old gods. Her conviction is given genuine depth. Beat: antagonist as true believer.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Canyon
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Voss's forces assault the roost; Bramble's wards fail, Ysolde falls holding the gate, and Pellam attempts the rite alone and is struck down. Beat: hope collapsing under fire.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dying Vaelith teaches Dominic the final verse of the choir-song and confesses the dragons chose silence long ago out of despair. Dominic must decide whether a world that broke its word deserves the fire back. Beat: the thematic crux — justice outside law, mercy beyond desert.

chapters.title: Fire Given Freely
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the altar, Dominic offers not her death but her name, her guild, her past — the rite accepts identity, not blood. The flame catches; Vaelith rises young again. Beat: climax, cost transmuted into transformation.

chapters.title: Judgment of the Waking
chapters.summary: Vaelith's POV. The waking dragon confronts Voss's army; rather than slaughter, the dragons demand truth. Voss, shown her own faith mirrored in dragonfire, breaks — some soldiers kneel, some flee. Beat: justice without vengeance.

chapters.title: After the Burning
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The valley reckons with the new age: shrines reopen, kingdoms send nervous envoys, and the surviving companions bury Ysolde and Osk together. Beat: tender aftermath, grief braided with wonder.

chapters.title: The First Priestess
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Offered restoration and titles, Dominic refuses them all; the covenant requires a keeper who belongs to no crown or guild. She chooses exile as wandering priestess, carrying embers to forgotten shrines. Beat: bittersweet resolve.

chapters.title: Choir Without End
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, epilogue. On a high pass a year later, Dominic hears the song answered from a dozen peaks — other keepers, other flames. Bramble and Pellam travel beside her; the family endures without walls. Final beat: survival was never the prize; belonging was.
